summary: bayes_diagnostics reported R-hat = 1.0 for constant chains, crashed on ties, and its ESS and quantile MCSE differed from Vehtari et al. (2021); the effective-count Barlow-Beeston fit accepted signed weights.

database_specific.introduced_basis: the defective lines are in the repository's first commit, the 0.3.0 import; earlier releases are not in this repository

observables: R-hat, bulk and tail ESS and quantile MCSE (bayes_diagnostics.py)
template_fit.py wbb fits with weighted templates
impact.bias: chains that never moved read as converged (R-hat 1.0); ESS and MCSE differed from ArviZ 0.23.4 by up to 0.7% and 7% for poorly mixed chains; chains with ties crashed the quantile MCSE; a template with negative weights was fitted by the effective-count likelihood, whose coverage fails there (0.526 for a 68% interval with 20% negative weights)
impact.trigger: stuck or constant chains, discrete (tied) draws, poorly mixed chains; templates from signed-weight Monte Carlo

remedy: rerun bayes_diagnostics.py (and any wbb-fit on signed-weight templates) with a release that has the fix (0.6.11 or later); a chain set reported converged before may now be not-converged
